description.from:
Behaviour spec for the versioned canonical evaluation representation that both gold loaders and scanner adapters emit before scoring.

The representation separates observation identity; exact semantic concept leaf and taxonomy ancestry; component type, subtype and instance/vendor; evidence locations; and display names. Display names and finding labels are never identity inputs.

```gherkin
Feature: Canonical evaluation representation
Scenario: Gold and scanner findings meet in one representation
  Given a corpus annotation and a scanner finding for the same evidence
  When each is loaded through its adapter
  Then both are canonical observations carrying the same contract version
  And identity, concept leaf, classification, instance and evidence are separate fields

Scenario: A display name cannot rescue a key mismatch
  Given a canonical expectation whose identity does not match a finding
  When the finding's display name equals the expectation's display name
  Then the observations do not match

Scenario: An ancestor concept is not an exact match
  Given an expectation whose concept leaf is a driver licence
  When a finding carries the national identifier ancestor concept
  Then exact-leaf correctness is not credited
  And ancestor-category correctness is reported separately
```

Blocked on the `subject.name` ruling, which decides what the source-name field receives per layer.
description.to:
Behaviour specification for the versioned canonical representation emitted by both gold and scanner adapters.

The representation separates repo-local observation/entity identity; asserted semantic concept leaf and ancestry; component type/subtype; optional asserted instance/vendor; evidence and derivation locations; observed-token candidates; and display text. Candidates, labels, and display names never rescue identity.

```gherkin
Feature: Canonical evaluation representation

Scenario: Gold and scanner findings meet in one representation
  Given canonical gold and a scanner finding for the same evidence
  When each passes through its adapter
  Then both carry the same contract version
  And entity identity, asserted classification, optional vendor and evidence are separate fields

Scenario: Legacy observed text cannot rescue a mismatch
  Given an expectation whose canonical identity does not match a finding
  When a display name or observed-token candidate happens to match
  Then the observations do not match

Scenario: Strict correctness uses asserted fields only
  Given an asset expectation asserting type and subtype but no instance
  When a finding matches the asserted fields and evidence
  Then strict correctness does not require the legacy display name

Scenario: Same-subtype components retain cardinality
  Given two database component expectations in one repository
  When both share a taxonomy subtype but have distinct canonical entities or evidence
  Then one finding cannot satisfy both expectations

Scenario: An ancestor concept is not an exact match
  Given an expectation whose concept leaf is driver licence
  When a finding carries only the national-identifier ancestor
  Then exact-leaf correctness is not credited
  And ancestor-category correctness is reported separately
```

Blocked on the legacy-name, component-instance, and component-cardinality rulings.
